expertInsight: Salesforce's current credential name is Salesforce Certified Marketing Cloud Account Engagement Specialist. This page uses “Pardot Specialist” as a legacy search label; current Salesforce materials call the product Account Engagement.

whoIsThisFor.heading: Who is the Account Engagement Specialist exam for?

personas.label: B2B marketing practitioners
personas.description: You use Account Engagement (Pardot) daily for email campaigns, forms, and lead nurturing and want to certify your hands-on skills.

personas.label: Marketing coordinators and specialists
personas.description: You configure automation rules, dynamic lists, and Engagement Studio programs and want formal recognition of your Pardot proficiency.

personas.label: Salesforce admins supporting marketing teams
personas.description: You manage the Pardot-Salesforce integration and want to validate your knowledge of prospect sync, scoring, and lead management.

examDifficulty.heading: Is the Account Engagement Specialist Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: The official exam guide covers visitors and prospects, administration, forms and landing pages, lead management, email marketing, and Engagement Studio.
bullets: 60 multiple-choice/multiple-select questions and up to five unscored questions in 90 minutes.
Exam objectives: Visitors and Prospects (8%), Administration (11%), Forms, Form Handlers and Landing Pages (20%), Lead Management (24%), Email Marketing (20%), and Engagement Studio (17%).
Preparation: Review how scoring, grading, automation, prospect records, and Salesforce integration work against the official objectives.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Use hands-on practice to review the official objectives. Build a sample Engagement Studio program, and explain scoring, grading, and prospect sync behavior.

examFormat.heading: Account Engagement Specialist Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: The exam is proctored online or in-person. Here is the format:
examFormat.scenarioPercent: The official guide does not publish a percentage of scenario-based questions. Practice applying its objectives to prospect, automation, forms, and Salesforce integration situations.
bestWayToPass: Know the automation hierarchy: Understand when to use completion actions (one-time, asset-specific), automation rules (continuous, criteria-based), and Engagement Studio (multi-step nurture programs).

Master scoring vs grading: Scoring measures engagement (activity-based), grading measures fit (attribute-based). Know scoring categories for multi-product tracking and grading profiles for ideal customer matching.

Study Pardot-Salesforce sync: Understand field sync behavior settings (Pardot wins, Salesforce wins, Most Recently Updated), the connector user’s permissions, and how prospects map to leads and contacts.

Practice forms and progressive profiling: Know the difference between Pardot Forms and Form Handlers, how progressive profiling works on repeat visits, and how completion actions trigger follow-up automations.

differentiation.heading: Account Engagement Specialist Traps & Readiness Checklist
differentiation.intro: These topics involve exact Account Engagement feature behavior as well as general marketing concepts.

commonTraps.trap: Treating completion actions, automation rules, and Engagement Studio as interchangeable
commonTraps.fix: Use completion actions for asset-specific one-time responses, automation rules for continuous criteria matching, and Engagement Studio for timed nurture journeys with branching.
Scoring measures engagement. Grading measures profile fit. Both signals can inform routing and sales follow-up decisions.
Know field sync behavior, connector user permissions, and when Salesforce, Account Engagement, or most recently updated values win.

commonTraps.trap: Choosing Pardot Forms when a Form Handler is required
commonTraps.fix: Use Pardot Forms for native hosted capture and progressive profiling; use Form Handlers when an existing external form must stay in place.

readinessBenchmarks: You can explain the difference between a dynamic list, segmentation list, suppression list, and automation rule without notes.
You have built at least one Engagement Studio program with wait steps, rules, and completion actions.
You can diagnose a prospect sync issue from field values, CRM ownership, and connector permissions.
You can explain the official objectives and review why each practice answer is correct.
whoShouldSkip: You have never configured Account Engagement assets or the Salesforce connector hands-on.
Your work is mostly Journey Builder, Automation Studio, or Email Studio; start with Marketing Cloud Email Specialist instead.

keyConcepts.h2: Pardot Specialist: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Scoring vs Grading: Interest vs Fit
blocks.body: **Scoring** is activity-based, it measures how interested a prospect is by tracking form submissions, email opens, page views, and file downloads. **Grading** is attribute-based, it measures how well a prospect fits your ideal customer profile (job title, company size, industry). Sales teams should prioritise prospects with both a high score (interest) and a high grade (fit). The official exam outline includes both scoring and grading under Lead Management.

blocks.heading: Automation Hierarchy: Completion Actions vs Automation Rules vs Engagement Studio
blocks.body: **Completion Actions** fire once when a prospect interacts with a specific asset (form submitted, email clicked). **Automation Rules** continuously evaluate all prospects against criteria and fire actions when criteria are met; they can run repeatedly. **Engagement Studio** is for time-based nurture with conditional branching, it combines wait steps and actions into a visual programme. Know when each is appropriate and when they overlap.

blocks.heading: Pardot-Salesforce Sync: Field Sync Behaviour
blocks.body: When Account Engagement and Salesforce hold different values for the same field, the field sync behaviour setting controls the outcome: Account Engagement wins, Salesforce wins, or Most Recently Updated wins. Each field can be configured independently. Practice tracing sync outcomes when CRM or marketing data should take precedence.

blocks.heading: Prospects and Visitors: Identification and Tracking
blocks.body: An anonymous website visitor becomes a Prospect when identified by email, via a form submission or a tracked email click that places a browser cookie. Pardot tracks all subsequent page views under that prospect record. **Dynamic Lists** automatically update membership as prospect attributes change. Scoring Categories maintain separate scores per product line. Know how each mechanism connects to prospect lifecycle stages.

blocks.heading: Pardot Forms vs Form Handlers
blocks.body: Pardot Forms are fully hosted by Pardot, they support progressive profiling (showing new fields on repeat visits), built-in validation, and native landing page embedding. Form Handlers connect Pardot to existing third-party forms on external websites, the visitor submits to the third-party form, which posts data to Pardot in the background. Use Form Handlers when you cannot replace an existing form; use Pardot Forms for new data capture assets.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce Marketing Cloud Account Engagement Specialist Exam
scenarioTips.intro: The Account Engagement Specialist exam tests hands-on configuration knowledge. Focus on the execution side, automation rules, dynamic lists, email sends, and form configuration, rather than high-level solution design.

blocks.heading: Automation Rules vs. Segmentation Rules
blocks.body: Automation Rules run continuously and apply actions retroactively to matching prospects. **Segmentation Rules** run once. Dynamic Lists update membership continuously based on criteria. Know which to use for each requirement.

blocks.heading: Email Configuration & Deliverability
blocks.body: Know the difference between **List Emails**, Engagement Studio emails, and Operational emails (bypass opt-out). Understand SPF, DKIM, and how sender score affects deliverability.

blocks.heading: Dynamic Content
blocks.body: Know how to configure dynamic content variations based on prospect fields (industry, score, etc.) for email personalization. Understand the default variation requirement and how dynamic content is inserted via HML or custom redirects.

blocks.heading: Forms & Progressive Profiling
blocks.body: Configure forms with dependent fields, progressive profiling (showing new fields on repeat visits), and Kiosk mode for events. Know how completion actions trigger follow-up automations.

blocks.heading: Pardot API & Integrations
blocks.body: Know the key Pardot API capabilities, how Pardot integrates with third-party tools via Zapier or direct API, and how the Salesforce-Pardot connector user's permission set controls data sync.

sampleQuestions.question: An anonymous website visitor fills in a form. What happens to them in Account Engagement?
options: They stay an anonymous visitor until a sales user converts them by hand
They are added to the next Engagement Studio program that happens to be running
They are created as a lead in Salesforce without any Account Engagement record
They become a prospect record
sampleQuestions.explanation: A visitor becomes a prospect once they are identified by email address, which a form submission supplies. The visitor activity already captured is then associated with that prospect.
whyWrong: Identification happens automatically on submission, with no manual step.
Program membership is a separate decision from identification.
The prospect record is created in Account Engagement first.

sampleQuestions.question: Which prospect behaviour feeds the score rather than the grade?
options: The size of the company the prospect works for as recorded on the account
The industry recorded on the prospect's own company record in the database
The job title that the prospect entered when they first completed a form
Opening an email and clicking its links
sampleQuestions.explanation: Score rises and falls with engagement activities such as email opens, link clicks, form submissions and page views. Grade is driven by profile attributes instead.
whyWrong: Company size is a profile attribute and affects grade.
Industry is a profile attribute and affects grade.
Job title is a profile attribute and affects grade.

sampleQuestions.question: A prospect has downloaded three whitepapers but works well outside the target market. How should this look?
options: A low score and a low grade because the company is outside the target market
High score, low grade
A low score and a high grade because of the company they happen to work for
A high score and an equally high grade because of the download activity
sampleQuestions.explanation: Scoring measures how interested a prospect is, and three downloads is real interest. Grading measures how well they fit the ideal customer profile, which here is poor.
whyWrong: The activity alone rules out a low score, whatever the fit.
Three downloads is substantial activity, so the score would not be low.
A high grade would mean the company matches the target profile, which it does not.

sampleQuestions.question: A company wants to keep its website forms exactly as they are but capture the submissions. What fits?
options: A landing page built in Account Engagement and linked from the website menu
A form handler
A dynamic list that is populated from the website's own submission database
An Account Engagement form embedded in place of the current website form
sampleQuestions.explanation: Form handlers accept posts from existing external forms, so the markup and styling you already have stay untouched while the data flows into Account Engagement.
whyWrong: A landing page hosts new content rather than preserving the current page.
Dynamic lists segment prospects and do not capture submissions.
An Account Engagement form would replace the existing form and its markup.

sampleQuestions.question: How do automation rules differ from completion actions?
options: Rules are configured by an administrator and completion actions by a marketer
Rules apply to prospects and completion actions apply to anonymous visitors
Rules look across the whole database; actions are tied to one asset
Rules run only once for each prospect whereas completion actions can run again
sampleQuestions.explanation: Automation rules continually check updated prospects across the database and can match again when a Repeat Rule is enabled. A completion action fires only on the asset it belongs to.
whyWrong: Either can be configured by anyone with the right permission.
Both work on prospects; neither targets anonymous visitors.
Repetition is a configuration choice rather than a fixed limit.

sampleQuestions.question: A marketer needs a one-time static list of prospects who match a set of criteria as of today. What should they use?
options: A segmentation rule
A completion action
A dynamic list
An automation rule
sampleQuestions.explanation: Segmentation rules run once against matching prospects and produce a fixed list.
whyWrong: Completion actions are tied to a single asset submission.
A dynamic list keeps updating, which is the opposite of a static snapshot.
Automation rules run on an ongoing basis rather than once.

sampleQuestions.question: A prospect is deleted in Salesforce but the record remains in Account Engagement. What is the expected sync behaviour?
options: Deletion does not cascade to Account Engagement
A duplicate prospect is created
The prospect is deleted immediately in both systems
The connector pauses until resolved
sampleQuestions.explanation: Deletion does not cascade from Salesforce to Account Engagement, so the prospect record persists.
whyWrong: No duplicate is produced by a deletion.
Deletions are not mirrored automatically.
The connector continues operating normally.

sampleQuestions.question: When a field value differs between Salesforce and Account Engagement, what normally decides the winner?
options: Whichever record was created first
The value is discarded in both systems
The field's sync behaviour setting
Account Engagement always wins
sampleQuestions.explanation: Each field has a configurable sync behaviour, and the default treats Salesforce as the system of record.
whyWrong: Creation order does not govern field conflicts.
Conflicts resolve to one value rather than clearing both.
Account Engagement winning is a configurable option, not the default.

sampleQuestions.question: How does Account Engagement normally convert a visitor into a prospect?
options: When the cookie expires
The visitor identifies themselves, usually via a form
After a set number of page views
Only once a sales user has created the record by hand
sampleQuestions.explanation: An anonymous visitor becomes a prospect once they supply identifying information, most commonly through a form.
whyWrong: Cookie expiry ends tracking rather than creating a prospect.
Page view volume alone does not identify anybody.
Manual creation is possible but is not the normal conversion path.

sampleQuestions.question: A company wants to keep its existing website form markup and styling exactly as it is, but capture submissions in Account Engagement. What fits?
options: A form handler
An Account Engagement form
A landing page
A dynamic list
sampleQuestions.explanation: Form handlers accept posts from a form you host and style yourself, leaving the existing markup untouched.
whyWrong: An Account Engagement form would replace the existing form and its markup.
A landing page hosts new content rather than preserving an existing page.
Dynamic lists segment prospects and do not capture submissions.

sampleQuestions.question: What is a trade-off of using a form handler rather than an Account Engagement form?
options: It cannot pass data to Salesforce
It requires a separate Engagement Studio licence to be bought
It cannot trigger completion actions
Progressive profiling and validation are unavailable
sampleQuestions.explanation: Features built into Account Engagement forms, including progressive profiling and native validation, are lost when you host the form yourself.
whyWrong: Form handlers do pass captured data through to Account Engagement and on to Salesforce.
No separate licence is involved.
Completion actions are available on form handlers.

sampleQuestions.question: What does progressive profiling achieve on a form?
options: It asks only for fields not yet captured
It scores the prospect twice
It hides the whole form from any prospect already known
It validates email syntax
sampleQuestions.explanation: Progressive profiling keeps forms short by requesting only fields not yet captured for that prospect.
whyWrong: Scoring is unrelated to field display.
The form remains available to known prospects with different fields.
Syntax validation is a separate form feature.

sampleQuestions.question: An Engagement Studio program should pause a prospect's path for three days before the next email. Which element does this?
options: A rule
A trigger
A wait step
An action step
sampleQuestions.explanation: Wait steps hold the prospect in place for a defined period before the program continues.
whyWrong: Rules branch on data the prospect already has.
Triggers branch on something the prospect does within a window.
Actions change data or send something.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the difference between a trigger and a rule in Engagement Studio?
options: A trigger is faster
A rule may only be used once in any single program
They behave identically
A trigger waits for behaviour; a rule checks data
sampleQuestions.explanation: Triggers listen for behaviour during a window, while rules evaluate existing prospect data immediately.
whyWrong: Speed is not the distinction.
There is no single-use restriction on rules.
They evaluate genuinely different things.

sampleQuestions.question: Scoring has been configured so that a pricing page visit adds more points than a blog visit. Why is this reasonable?
options: Scores must always differ between pages
Blog pages are not tracked by default
Pricing interest signals stronger buying intent
Pricing pages load more quickly than the blog pages do
sampleQuestions.explanation: Scoring is meant to reflect how much an action indicates intent, and pricing interest indicates more than casual reading.
whyWrong: Equal weighting is allowed; the point is that weight should reflect intent.
Blog visits are tracked and can carry points.
Load speed has nothing to do with scoring.

sampleQuestions.question: A marketer wants different content shown inside one email depending on the prospect's industry. What should they use?
options: A segmentation rule
Dynamic content
A separate email per industry
A form handler
sampleQuestions.explanation: Dynamic content varies a region of the email based on prospect field values, keeping it to a single asset.
whyWrong: Segmentation rules build lists rather than varying content within an email.
Building one email per industry multiplies maintenance for the same result.
Form handlers capture submissions and do not affect email content.

introLead.text: This guide covers Marketing Cloud Account Engagement work across prospects, lead qualification, forms, email, automation, and reporting. Its 15 sample questions check prospect records, scoring versus grading, and forms versus form handlers. Compare the practice set with Salesforce's
